messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - 1871234567 - multi-region error surge detected in eu-west-1, 5xx/429 increase > 4x baseline, triggered SLO pager.

maya: seeing steady 429s and request queueing on provider-B nodes in eu-west-1, median latency up ~300ms. error-rate spikes started ~10m ago.

sanjay: confirmed provider-B node pool saturated; their telemetry shows backend throttling on our traffic prefixes. router logs: `upstream 503` and `rate_limited`.

eli: also seeing large increase in model KV-cache misses for long-history chat sessions — amplifies cost. suspect combined load + provider-side rate caps.

maya: mitigation plan: 1) immediate soft rate limit on non-critical traffic (reranks, experimental features) 2) steer production traffic from provider-B -> provider-A in eu-west 3) partial brownout: disable `reranker-v2` for 30m 4) if pressure persists, region failover to eu-central for critical customers.

ruth: support is getting 3 escalations from customers complaining about slow responses and errors; highest priority customer is tenant:acme-inc (SLA). Notifying them now.

maya: @ruth thanks. mark acme-inc as critical, make sure we keep them on primary path if possible.

eli: commands I recommend:
```bash
# soft limit reranks to 50%
redwoodctl traffic update --region eu-west-1 --route rerank --rate 50%
# disable experimental reranker
redwoodctl feature toggle --region eu-west-1 --feature reranker-v2 --state off
# provider reroute (gradual)
redwoodctl provider route --region eu-west-1 --from provider-B --to provider-A --weight 0.7 --step 10
```

sanjay: executing step 1 and 2 now. will do gradual routing to avoid overload on provider-A.

deploy-bot: deploy pipeline triggered: `traffic-shape/eu-west-1/1871234567` started by sanjay. CI checks ok.

maya: sanjay please apply the rerank rate limit first, then toggle the feature. do provider reroute only once rate limit reduces backpressure.

sanjay: applied rerank rate limit -> 50%. config diff: `routes.rerank.rate: 100% -> 50%`.

eli: feature toggle performed: `reranker-v2` -> OFF in eu-west-1. Observability note: token-level cost should drop.

maya: monitoring: 429s dropped ~30% in last 3m, latency improving but still ~2.1x baseline. provider-A accepting traffic (routing step 1).

sanjay: route step 1 -> weight 0.7 to provider-A applied. provider-A CPU up ~18% but within thresholds.

ruth: update: acme-inc reported transient failures earlier but now only slow responses. they're in the loop, appreciate updates.

maya: good. keep throttles on reranks until we see stable 15m window. Next actions: prepare for partial brownout of non-critical features if we see re-escalation. also prepare failover playbook if provider-A degrades.

eli: posting quick health check snippet for drill:
```json
{
  "eu-west-1": {
    "provider-A": "healthy",
    "provider-B": "degraded",
    "reranker": "disabled",
    "rerank_rate": "50%"
  }
}
```

rotation-bot: oncall handoff scheduled in 22m to user `maya` -> `sanjay`. please acknowledge.

maya: acknowledged handoff note. I'll be primary until handoff; sanjay you take second.

sanjay: ack. I'll monitor provider-A tail latency and backpressure metrics.

maya: we're seeing a small uptick in 5xx from a subset of customers routed to provider-A (long context sessions). decision: apply selective quota caps for long-context (>4k tokens) sessions for 15m to ease memory pressure.

eli: suggested command: `redwoodctl quota update --region eu-west-1 --scope long_context --limit 3rps` then reevaluate.

sanjay: applied quota caps for long-context sessions.

ruth: running quick customer-impact triage: affected tenants list = [acme-inc, betaworks, media-x]. acme-inc on critical path, others notified.

maya: thanks. start incident ticket INC-18712 and mark severity S3 -> S2 if acme-inc SLA at risk.

incident-bot: INC-18712 created by maya. Severity: S2. Link: https://redwood/incident/INC-18712

maya: after quota cap and routing, 5xx rate down 65%, 429s stable ~baseline. latency back to ~1.2x baseline for most customers.

ruth: acme-inc acknowledged and will keep monitoring; they requested a post-incident summary.

eli: let's keep reranker disabled for 45m total, then ramp to 25% and observe with canary traffic.

sanjay: agree. I'll schedule a canary ramp at +45m if metrics remain good.

maya: preparing mitigation summary for followups: steps taken, timing, customer impact, follow-up tasks (postmortem, runbook updates).

maya: any objections to de-escalating paging after handoff and continued watch?

ruth: support fine with watch mode; will escalate if customer complaints increase.

rotation-bot: handoff executed: maya -> sanjay at ts +22m.

sanjay: taking over. continuing watch, will close if stable for 1h.

eli: action items for postmortem: 1) evaluate provider-B circuit limits, 2) improve rerank fallback logic to auto-fallback to reranker-v1, 3) add a playbook snippet for selective long-context quotas.

maya: adding notes to INC-18712 and assigning tasks. thanks everyone.

deploy-bot: traffic-shape/eu-west-1/1871234567 completed successfully.

sanjay: closing thread for now, will reopen if we see new spikes.

maya: thanks all :thumbsup:
